Consult Summary:
- The patient presents with acute, progressively worsening lower abdominal pain (constant, about 8/10) with light vaginal bleeding and light pink discharge; an in-person abdominal examination is planned, along with a pregnancy test today and follow-up based on findings.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute, lower abdominal pain in the midline/lower abdomen, started a few days ago, gradually worsening and currently constant (pain reported as 8/10). Associated light vaginal bleeding and light pink discharge.
- Pain characteristics: Constant, not clearly relieved by anything mentioned; worsens over days.
- Gastrointestinal: Past week constipation that resolved this week; bowel movements currently reported as normal.
- Gynecologic/ obstetric history: On a contraceptive implant (Implanon). Menstrual pattern described as irregular on implant; last menstrual period was approximately 2–3 weeks ago. At one point the patient stated the period had stopped about 2 weeks ago, with current light pink discharge noted.
- Pregnancy-related: Had a pregnancy test about one month ago. Willing to have a pregnancy test performed today; if positive, urgent review advised.
- Nausea/vomiting: Nausea present; no vomiting.
- Urinary symptoms: No dysuria or significant urinary changes reported; drinks fluids regularly; reports variable urinary frequency not clearly outlined.
- Sexual activity/ contraception: Sexually active; last intercourse approximately four days ago. Uses Implanon for contraception.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Travel: Has traveled abroad about a year ago (no recent travel reported).

Past Medical History:
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Chronic conditions: None documented.
- Surgeries: None documented.
- Pregnancies: None documented.

Medications:
- Contraceptive implant (Implanon).
- No other medications listed.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (documented).

Social History:
- Occupation: School teacher.
- Living situation: Lives with husband and husband’s family.
- Smoking/alcohol/drug use: Not clearly known from transcript.
- Travel: Abroad about a year ago.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Exam findings: Not provided.

Investigations:
- Pregnancy testing: To be performed today.
- Prior pregnancy test: Performed about one month ago.
- Other labs/imaging: Not documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute lower abdominal pain, worsening over several days.
  - Plan:
    - Proceed with face-to-face abdominal examination in clinic to further evaluate cause.
    - If symptoms worsen, or if the patient cannot tolerate oral intake or fluids, seek urgent review.
    - Contact the support line to arrange the clinic appointment.
    - Reassess after examination with management guidance based on findings.

- Issue 2: Intermittent vaginal bleeding with light pink discharge; irregular menses on Implanon.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain pregnancy test today.
    - If pregnancy test positive, arrange urgent follow-up.
    - If negative, follow-up planning contingent on clinical exam results and further evaluation in clinic.

- Issue 3: Contraception considerations (Implanon) and menstrual pattern changes.
  - Plan:
    - Document bleeding pattern related to Implanon; manage according to clinic assessment results.
    - Continue contraception as currently used unless advised otherwise after evaluation.

- General Plan:
  - If symptoms worsen or patient cannot tolerate fluids, seek urgent care before scheduled appointment.
  - If pregnancy test is positive, immediate escalation advised.
  - If pregnancy test is negative, proceed with in-clinic evaluation and management.

Document Quality:
- Missing elements: Vital signs; detailed physical examination findings; full medication list with doses; laboratory/imaging results beyond pregnancy testing.
- Conflicts within transcript: Inconsistent statements about last menstrual period (two weeks ago vs. 2–3 weeks ago) and whether the period stopped. Conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Some phrases were garbled (e.g., travel and location details), and some questions/answers were unclear or incomplete. No definitive vitals or imaging results were recorded.
